Here's the blunt version: I don't care what the textbook says my "lane" is. I care about the patient in front of me. If a kid comes in with a fever and a rash, and I don't know the difference between meningococcemia and a viral exanthem, I'm not a good emergency physician. I'm a liability.

I draw on everything I know—internal medicine, pediatrics, surgery, toxicology—because emergencies don't respect departmental boundaries. If I can't answer it, I say so. But I don't hide behind a specialty label to avoid doing the work.
